title: The One-Tap Google Review System (From the Podcast)
meta: The simple system to get more Google reviews without feeling desperate: ask at the peak, send a one-tap link within the hour, and ask everyone — never gate.
short: Get more reviews with three moves: ask at peak gratitude, make it one tap, and ask everyone. No bribes, no gating — just a habit bolted onto the end of every job.
statLabel: The friction budget for a review request — every extra step loses you responses

body.answer: Peak timing + one tap + ask everyone. That's the whole system.
body.html: Most shops 'ask for reviews' by hoping. The ones that win make it a system: ask at the peak, remove all friction, and ask every single customer. No incentives, no gating — just a repeatable habit that runs on autopilot.

body.answer: Ask the moment the job's done and they're happy.
body.html: The window is short. The instant the work is finished and the customer is thrilled — that's when they'll leave a review. Wait until tomorrow and the feeling (and the intent) is gone. Bake the ask into the end of the job itself.

body.h2: One tap, sent within the hour
body.answer: Text the direct link — don't make them search.
body.html: Every extra step bleeds responses. Text the direct Google review link within the hour so it's one tap from 'sure' to done. Don't hand them a card and hope they Google you later — most won't.

body.answer: Filtering for happy customers only violates Google's policy.
body.html: Asking only the customers you think are happy ('gating') is against Google's rules and it's transparent to anyone watching your review pattern. Ask everyone. A genuinely good shop earns a genuinely good rating.

body.answer: This one came straight off the podcast.
body.html: Marshall and Ray went deep on this in Get More Google Reviews on Get Booked, Not F***ed — same math, more cussing. Watch or listen to the full episode here.

faq.q: How do I get more Google reviews?
faq.a: Ask at peak gratitude (job just finished), send a one-tap review link within the hour, and ask every customer — no gating, no bribes.

faq.q: Can I offer a discount for reviews?
faq.a: No. Paying for or incentivizing reviews violates Google's policies and can get your profile penalized. Just ask, consistently.

faq.q: When is the best time to ask for a review?
faq.a: The moment the job is done and the customer is happy. Timing beats everything — waiting even a day sharply lowers response rates.
